vkinder.title: VKinder
vkinder.status: Core team project · Applied data science
vkinder.summary: Help families and practitioners explore how place shapes childhood across Greater Melbourne. A team-built platform connects neighbourhood evidence, family-priority matching and an exploratory school-entry forecast.
vkinder.result: 346 reporting areas · 8 family priorities · 6.43 percentage-point forecast MAE
vkinder.alt: VKinder evidence summary: 346 Melbourne reporting areas, eight family priorities, and ridge forecast MAE of 6.43 percentage points compared with persistence at 7.56
vkinder.caption: Model-card results: 2021–2024 chronological test, 342 areas. Lower forecast error is better; this is area-level research, not an individual child prediction.
steps: Public development, environment and service data
vkinder.scope: Core team project, also named KinderPrint in the repository. Includes data pipelines, an area-matching engine and a web application. The source repository is private.
vkinder.failure: One test transition shares a Melbourne-wide shift. Ridge over-predicts by 3.48 percentage points; nominal 80% intervals cover only 69.9%. Historical origins reuse IRSD 2021, and 2027 interval coverage is not demonstrated. Findings are exploratory, not causal or diagnostic.
vkinder.scale: The model card reports 346 areas, with all eight needs scored for 330. Chronological evaluation reports ridge MAE of 6.43 percentage points versus 7.56 for persistence on 342 test areas, a 14.9% reduction. These are repository-reported results, not a new independent rerun.
vkinder.cost: The documented deployment uses Vercel for the frontend and AWS Lambda, API Gateway and RDS PostgreSQL for the API and data. No hosting-cost or production-latency benchmark is claimed.
vkinder.security: Area-level indicators do not assess individual children. Missing measures remain missing; data gates reject invalid refreshes and restore prior outputs. The documented API uses a read-only database role.
vkinder.reason: When a friend and I were looking at places to move, we tried to find useful information about neighbourhood health patterns. We couldn't find something that helped us compare areas clearly. That gap became the starting point for VKinder. The project now focuses on area-level child development, environment and services; it doesn't assess personal health risks.
vkinder.whatWentWrong: The model card records a shortlist-stability bug: an earlier version re-ranked only initially eligible areas, overstating stability. The corrected version reruns the complete search. The forecast also missed a Melbourne-wide shift; its nominal 80% intervals covered only 69.9% of test areas.
vkinder.nextStep: I'd prioritise past-only socioeconomic inputs and more chronological evaluation before presenting the outlook more confidently. A lower average error doesn't fix poorly calibrated uncertainty.

voltwise.title: Voltwise
voltwise.summary: Forecast battery capacity ten discharge cycles ahead from NASA laboratory measurements. Compare held-out predictions against a persistence baseline and inspect the tested analytics pipeline.
voltwise.result: 0.024 Ah MAE · 560 held-out windows · 44.7% lower error than persistence
voltwise.alt: Recorded capacity degradation of NASA laboratory battery B0005 over 168 discharge cycles
voltwise.caption: NASA laboratory cell B0005: 168 recorded discharge cycles. Capacity is measured in ampere-hours (Ah).
voltwise.scope: Implemented pipeline; the Ollama agent and FastAPI service run locally.
voltwise.failure: Cell-level holdout limits leakage between training and evaluation. Data checks reject invalid forecast populations. Four laboratory cells do not establish vehicle-fleet reliability.
voltwise.scale: Four cells and 560 held-out forecast windows. No production throughput or latency benchmark is claimed.
voltwise.cost: The public dashboard is static. Running the local model and agent uses your own computer; no hosted LLM service is required.
voltwise.security: The local agent exposes bounded read-only metric tools, not arbitrary SQL, shell access or data writes.
voltwise.reason: Batteries gave this project a practical question: can we forecast capacity loss early enough to make the next measurement less of a surprise? The appeal is that a prediction can be checked against real measurements and a simple baseline. This is a small laboratory study, not a vehicle-ready model.
voltwise.whatWentWrong: The main risk is an easy evaluation. Neighbouring windows from the same cell share history, so a random row split can make the model look better than it is. This pipeline holds out whole batteries. That still leaves only four laboratory cells, not evidence of performance on vehicles.
voltwise.nextStep: I'd test on more cells and different operating conditions before adding model complexity. I'd also check how error changes as the forecast horizon grows, rather than reporting one average.

senseway.title: Sensory-Aware Route Planner
senseway.summary: Calculate walking routes on a real central-Melbourne street graph. Pedestrian-counter snapshots add context only when freshness and reporting-coverage checks pass.
senseway.alt: Screenshot of the live Melbourne route planner with mapped walking streets and a calculated path
senseway.caption: Actual demo, 1 November 2026. Map: © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL). Council data: City of Melbourne (CC BY).
senseway.scope: Implemented static demo. Retained AWS backend code is a separate, undeployed path.
senseway.failure: Stale counters are excluded. With no eligible observations, activity-based routing is unavailable while shortest-path routing still works. Noise and lighting remain unknown.
senseway.scale: CBD extract: 16,386 connected nodes and 18,772 segments. This is data coverage, not measured user impact or routing latency.
senseway.cost: GitHub Pages serves static JSON and JavaScript. There is no live database or paid routing API in this demo.
senseway.security: Address search and route calculation run in the browser. Journeys are not submitted to a remote routing service.
senseway.reason: I'm more comfortable with a bit of chaos than with silence. That made me think about someone who feels the opposite: what if noise makes a walk difficult? This was a way to look beyond my own preferences. The current prototype uses pedestrian activity where the data is reliable; it can't yet measure how noisy or comfortable a route will feel.
senseway.whatWentWrong: The available data cannot support live noise or light claims. Pedestrian counters can be stale or incomplete. When those checks fail, the app disables activity-based routing rather than pretending it has a quieter route.
senseway.nextStep: I'd evaluate route choices with people who have sensory access needs, then add measured noise and lighting only where reliable observations exist. Crowd counts alone aren't a sensory-accessibility score.

nexora.title: Nexora (DataMedic)
nexora.summary: Step through pipeline diagnosis and recovery using recorded synthetic scenarios. The demo explains investigation steps; it does not repair a live data platform.
nexora.result: Recorded scenarios only. No production recovery-time benchmark.
nexora.scope: Public repository contains compiled assets and synthetic results, not an operational backend.
nexora.failure: A recorded recovery cannot demonstrate recovery from unseen incidents. A live diagnostic engine would need separate integration and evaluation.
nexora.scale: No measured production latency, throughput or recovery rate is published.
nexora.cost: Static demo with no database or running backend.
nexora.security: No company data or credentials are included. Browser selections are temporary.
nexora.reason: Pipeline failures are easier to discuss when you can step through an example. Nexora, previously DataMedic, makes that investigation visible with synthetic scenarios.
nexora.whatWentWrong: Recorded recovery playback cannot show that an engine will recover from an unseen incident. This public demo has no operational backend or measured production recovery time.
nexora.nextStep: I'd connect one real, reproducible test pipeline and measure diagnosis accuracy and failed recoveries before expanding the demo.

wildlife.title: Wildlife Detection API
wildlife.summary: An image-inference API architecture combining YOLOv8, FastAPI and container deployment. The repository documents validation, readiness probes and infrastructure configuration.
wildlife.result: No published wildlife mAP or reproducible latency result. Not featured as a measured outcome.
wildlife.scope: Architecture follows the repository documentation. No current public endpoint is verified.
wildlife.failure: Readiness checks prevent traffic before model startup. ONNX has a PyTorch fallback. Task-specific accuracy and overload behaviour still need evaluation.
wildlife.scale: Replica configuration and Locust tooling are documented; a completed load-test result is not supplied.
wildlife.cost: OCI compute and Kubernetes hosting would require provisioning and a separate cost estimate. No running cloud cost is claimed.
wildlife.security: Authentication, rate limiting, scanning and production observability are listed as future work in the repository.
wildlife.reason: An image model needs an API, validation and a deployment path before another application can use it. This repository explores that surrounding engineering.
wildlife.whatWentWrong: The architecture is documented, but there is no published wildlife accuracy benchmark or reproducible latency result. Deployment configuration alone does not establish model quality.
wildlife.nextStep: I'd start with a labelled wildlife evaluation set and publish precision, recall and latency before spending more time on infrastructure.

speech.title: Speech Analysis Tool
speech.summary: A proposed speech-feedback tool covering sentiment, speech rate, grammar and pronunciation. The current repository describes the idea, without a validated implementation.
speech.result: No measured model quality or operational demo. Retained as an early concept.
speech.scope: Conceptual flow from the README, not a deployed system.
speech.failure: No evaluation dataset, error analysis or performance results are supplied.
speech.cost: No deployed service; costs are not established.
speech.security: Any future implementation would require consent, retention limits and protection for submitted speech. It is not an employment-assessment system.
speech.reason: The proposed tool explores whether speech feedback could be understandable and useful to a learner. It remains a concept.
speech.whatWentWrong: There is no validated implementation or evaluation dataset, so there is no working outcome to report yet.
speech.nextStep: I'd narrow the first version to one feedback task and evaluate it with consenting users before adding more features.
